title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_238.txt
concise_summary: PKD theorizes that his precognitive faculty allowed him to foresee his death via the Xerox missive crisis of early 1974, and that he successfully overcome predetermined fate by consciously accessing precognitive knowledge through his unconscious mind. He argues this was either divine intervention via VALIS or a biological mechanism of collective unconscious memory; time itself may have halted or reversed to allow him to simultaneously experience death and survival.
key_claims: Precognition is a survival mechanism that allows one to foresee fatal situations and derive information from the foreseen failure to ultimately succeed
PKD's death in early 1974 was real at a metaphysical level; part of him passed into postmortem eternity while he remained physically alive
The Xerox missive crisis was solvable only through a two-pass model: first failure yielded essential information, second attempt succeeded with that knowledge
VALIS is either a master controlling entity moving retrograde in time, or a manifestation of reality running backward when forward time is abolished
The 'Thomas' consciousness that seized control of PKD during the crisis is his own precognitive unconscious made conscious, with knowledge from the collective unconscious
Divine Providence or biological quantum-leap evolution, or both, provided the mechanism for PKD to overcome heimarmene (fate)
recurring_concepts: Thomas (the unconscious alter-ego with precog knowledge)

tensions: How can precognition foresee only the failure, not the success? PKD admits his precognition didn't foresee solution B, only failure A

Time had run out; how could my precog faculty look forward any more? There was no more time for me! And what event would be more important to scan in advance than your death, especially when you didn't merely die but were slain, and by a trap, which, had you been able to figure it out, you would have survived (there was a way out); so in my writing in the Sixties I analyze the trap again and again, searching for the solution. I was successful (as represented in THE PENULTIMATE TRUTH); notify the authorities. This is utterly opposite from Jones' precog faculty in THE WORLD JONES MADE, where his precog faculty didn't help him avoid his death. Okay; as soon as I handled the Xerox missive crisis, a future opened up for me where, in the world that I didn't handle the Xerox missive crisis, there was no future; so all at once tremendous amounts of information from the new for-the-first-time future poured over me, all sorts of precog material: I had set up an alternate future by successfully handling the Xerox missive. This is why I always said, "I lived through the Xerox missive crisis twice, the first time failing to solve it, the second time successfully solving it based on knowlede derived from the first time." It was my original involvement foreseen by my precognition, this involvement having the aspect of a rigid determinism that I was overpowering. It had the aspect of fate. I had to fail, which yielded me the information I needed, and then I relived in utilizing that information. This is why I had information that I could not possibly (normally) have had, information THAT WOULD ONLY DEVELOP --COME INTO BEING-- LATER WHEN IT WOULD BE TOO LATE. The trap, then, was so constructed that you could only develop the essential information by failing to escape; you would then know what you needed to know. Providence saw how it could be solved: through precognition of faulty solution A. Through, literally tracking the situation twice. The paradox was: You could only get the information by which to succeed BY FAILING. Seeing the fish produced a shock of recognition on my part, an instant and powerful one that resonnated on an unconscious level.
